title_en: Chikan Township Enterprise Supply and Marketing Corporation v. Darong Industrial Trade Corporation and Others — dispute over compensation for tort damages
keywords_en: civil; dispute over tort damages; first instance; basic people's court; Guangdong Province; Hainan Province; Heilongjiang Province; legal person; General Principles of the Civil Law; infringement of rights of joint purchasers; forging an agreement and unilateral receipt of goods; statute of limitations; steel billet purchase and sale contract; advance payment; forging a supplementary agreement; unilateral extraction of goods; good faith; dispute over tort damages involving the head office, etc.
full_text_en:
Chikan Township Enterprise Supply and Marketing General Corporation v. Darong Industrial and Trade General Corporation et al. — dispute over compensation for tortious damage

Plaintiff: Chikan Township Enterprise Supply and Marketing General Corporation of Zhanjiang City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Liang Taofeng, General Manager of the Corporation.

Agent ad litem: Ou Zhihui, Legal Advisor of Chikan Township Enterprise Supply and Marketing General Corporation of Zhanjiang City, Guangdong Province.

Agent ad litem: Liang Guixing, Deputy Manager of Zhanjiang City Materials General Corporation, Guangdong Province.

Defendant: Hainan Darong Industrial and Trade General Corporation.

Legal Representative: Tong Maosheng, General Manager of the Corporation.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Wei, Lawyer of Hailian Law Firm.

Defendant: Heilongjiang International Economic and Technical Trade Corporation.

Legal Representative: Nie Zhiyu, Manager of the Corporation.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Yannian, Lawyer of Jinma Law Firm of Heilongjiang Province.

The plaintiff, Chikan Township Enterprise Supply and Marketing General Corporation of Zhanjiang City, Guangdong Province (hereinafter referred to as Chikan Company), filed a lawsuit with the Xinhua District People's Court of Haikou City, Hainan Province, against the defendants, Hainan Darong Industrial and Trade General Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Darong Company) and Heilongjiang International Economic and Technical Trade Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Heilongjiang Company), regarding a dispute over compensation for tortious damage.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The defendant Darong Company, in collusion with the defendant Heilongjiang Company, which was the supplier under the contract, infringed upon the legitimate rights and interests that the plaintiff, as a co-buyer under the contract, should enjoy; Heilongjiang Company, to facilitate the success of Darong Company's infringing act, intentionally breached the contract by supplying goods, causing losses to the plaintiff. The plaintiff requests the court to order: 1. Darong Company to return the prepaid货款 of RMB 2,000,000 to the plaintiff and compensate the plaintiff for interest losses at a monthly interest rate of 4%, with Heilongjiang Company bearing joint and several liability for this debt of Darong Company; 2. Heilongjiang Company to compensate the plaintiff for losses at 5% of the total contract amount for breach of contract; 3. Darong Company and Heilongjiang Company to jointly compensate the plaintiff for the expenses of RMB 172,400 incurred in pursuing the goods and the money; 4. Darong Company and Heilongjiang Company to bear the litigation costs of this case.

Defendant Darong Company's Defense: 1. The tripartite contract stipulated that the defendant Heilongjiang Company would supply 25,000 tons of steel billets to the plaintiff Chikan Company and the defendant Darong Company. Darong Company was a co-buyer under the contract and had paid a prepayment of RMB 3,000,000. Based on the proportion of prepayments made by Darong Company and Chikan Company, Darong Company was entitled to receive 15,000 tons of steel billets, but in fact Darong Company only received 2,000 tons, far less than the tonnage it should have received, and did not cause any economic losses to Chikan Company. Chikan Company's legitimate rights and interests should be realized by requiring Heilongjiang Company to continue supplying the goods. 2. Chikan Company learned on September 8, 1993, that Darong Company had received 2,000 tons of steel billets. If Chikan Company believed that this act of Darong Company infringed upon its legitimate rights and interests, it should have asserted its rights within the two-year statute of limitations. In fact, Chikan Company did not file this tort action until January 21, 1997, which exceeds the statute of limitations. The court should dismiss Chikan Company's claims.

Defendant Heilongjiang Company's Defense: 1. Regarding the issue of the 2,000 tons of goods being taken by the defendant Darong Company, the written correspondence at the time confirms this, and although some of the correspondence was forged by Darong Company, Heilongjiang Company was unaware of this and did not collude with Darong Company. Heilongjiang Company did not infringe upon the legitimate rights and interests of the plaintiff Chikan Company and should not bear joint and several liability for Darong Company's actions. 2. Regarding whether Heilongjiang Company breached the contract, in the previous lawsuit filed by Chikan Company, the Guangdong High People's Court has already determined that all three parties to the contract were in breach and may not pursue liability for breach of contract against each other. 3. Heilongjiang Company did not cause losses to Chikan Company and should not bear Chikan Company's expenses for pursuing the money and goods or the litigation costs.

Xinhua District People's Court of Haikou City found the following facts upon trial:

On May 11, 1993, the plaintiff Chikan Company and the defendant Darong Company, as co-buyers, entered into a steel billet purchase and sales contract with the defendant Heilongjiang Company, stipulating: Heilongjiang Company would supply 25,000 tons of steel billets to Chikan Company and Darong Company; the buyers would first prepay RMB 5,000,000; the supplier would deliver all goods by June 27, 1993. On May 12, Chikan Company prepaid RMB 2,000,000, and Darong Company prepaid RMB 3,000,000. The parties did not make any written agreement on how to distribute the steel billets upon arrival.

After receiving the prepayment of RMB 5,000,000, the defendant Heilongjiang Company was unable to deliver the goods on time. On July 8, the plaintiff Chikan Company and the defendant Darong Company entered into a modification agreement with Heilongjiang Company, stipulating: 1. The 2,000 tons of 80×80×1050 A3 steel billets in transit from the supplier would be delivered to the buyers at Tianjin Port on July 15 as the first batch; the 5,859 tons of 60×60×11620 A3 steel billets in 93 railway cars in transit would be delivered to the buyers at Zhanjiang Port by the end of July as the second batch; the remaining 17,141 tons of steel billets would be delivered within one and a half months; 2. If the supplier breached, it would pay the buyers bank interest at a monthly rate of 4% on the prepayment of RMB 5,000,000, and also pay compensation to the buyers at 5% of the total contract transaction amount. If the buyers breached, they would pay compensation to the supplier at 5% of the total contract transaction amount; 3. After receiving the first batch of steel billets, the buyers would recover the prepayment in proportion to the actual quantity received. When the second batch began to be shipped, the payment for the first batch would be settled in full; 4. Any terms of the original contract not modified would remain in effect.

After the modification agreement was signed, the defendant Darong Company forged a "Supplementary Agreement" between itself and the plaintiff Chikan Company in July and faxed it to the defendant Heilongjiang Company. The forged agreement stated: the first batch of 2,000 tons of steel billets would be received by Darong Company upon arrival at Tianjin; Chikan Company's General Manager Liang Taofeng and Darong Company's Xu Zuotian would go to Dalian together to sign the sales contract for these 2,000 tons of steel billets, and the货款 would be returned to Darong Company before July 16.

On July 31, the plaintiff Chikan Company sent a letter to the defendant Heilongjiang Company stating: the 2,000 tons of steel billets at Tianjin Port should be received and settled by Chikan Company in conjunction with the defendant Darong Company with joint signatures; neither party had the right to receive the goods alone. If the failure to receive the goods on time was due to reasons attributable to Chikan Company and Darong Company, Chikan Company would bear the consequences.

On August 8, the defendant Darong Company, in its own name and by impersonating the plaintiff Chikan Company, entered into a purchase and sales contract with the defendant Heilongjiang Company, stipulating: Heilongjiang Company would supply 2,000 tons of steel billets to Darong Company and Chikan Company at a unit price of RMB 2,650 per ton, for a total amount of RMB 5,300,000. After Heilongjiang Company delivered the bill of lading to Darong Company and Chikan Company, Darong Company and Chikan Company would pay Heilongjiang Company the outstanding balance of RMB 300,000 after deducting the prepayment. This contract bore the seals of Heilongjiang Company and Darong Company.

On August 18, the defendant Darong Company paid RMB 300,000 to the defendant Heilongjiang Company. On September 1, Darong Company delivered a receipt for goods to Heilongjiang Company. The receipt stated: received 2,000 tons of 80×80 steel billets from Heilongjiang Company. The recipient's place bore the seals of Darong Company and the plaintiff Chikan Company. Among these, the seal and signature of Chikan Company were forged by Darong Company. On the same day, Heilongjiang Company, based on this receipt, delivered the 2,000 tons of steel billets to Darong Company at Tianjin Port. After receiving these 2,000 tons of steel billets, Darong Company sold them all and retained all the sales proceeds.

On September 15, the plaintiff Chikan Company sent a letter to the defendant Heilongjiang Company, pointing out that the goods should be received by Chikan Company and the defendant Darong Company simultaneously, that Darong Company could not unilaterally receive the goods based on a forged agreement, and that Heilongjiang Company should recover the 2,000 tons of steel billets already delivered to Darong Company. On September 18, Darong Company sent a letter to Heilongjiang Company, stating that the economic liability arising from the 2,000-ton steel billet transaction would be resolved through negotiation between Darong Company and Chikan Company, and that Heilongjiang Company need not bear any responsibility. Accordingly, on September 20, Heilongjiang Company sent a letter to Chikan Company stating: Whether Darong Company forged documents, Heilongjiang Company is unclear and will not bear responsibility; Chikan Company should resolve this issue through friendly negotiation with Darong Company.

On November 21, the defendant Heilongjiang Company sent a letter to the plaintiff Chikan Company stating: 5,000 tons of 60×60×11620 steel billets have arrived at the Tianjin warehouse; due to an increase in price by the Russian party, the price per ton is RMB 2,450; we now notify your company to bring funds to Tianjin to take delivery within five days. Chikan Company believed that Heilongjiang Company had not supplied the goods at the time, place, and price stipulated in the contract and refused to take delivery.

On December 15, 1993, the plaintiff Chikan Company filed a lawsuit with the Zhanjiang Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province on the grounds that the defendant Heilongjiang Company had failed to supply the goods as stipulated in the contract, and also named Darong Company as a third party in the action. Chikan Company requested the court to order Heilongjiang Company to return the prepayment of RMB 2,000,000 and pay interest at the agreed monthly rate of 4%, pay liquidated damages at 5% of the total contract transaction amount, and compensate for the expenses of RMB 70,000 incurred in pursuing the money. On August 18, 1995, the Zhanjiang Intermediate People's Court entered a judgment: 1. The steel billet purchase and sales contract and its modification agreement were terminated; 2. Darong Company was ordered to return RMB 2,000,000 to Chikan Company plus interest (interest calculated from May 12, 1993, until the effective date of this judgment, at a monthly rate of 4%); 3. Darong Company was ordered to compensate Chikan Company for the loss of RMB 70,000 in pursuing the money; 4. The litigation costs of RMB 23,360 were to be borne by Darong Company. Darong Company appealed the first-instance judgment. On second instance, the Guangdong High People's Court held: The steel billet purchase and sales contract and its modification agreement were legally established. Heilongjiang Company's delivery of the 2,000 tons of steel billets to Darong Company should be deemed as the buyers having received 2,000 tons of goods. After receiving the first batch of goods, the buyers failed to pay the full amount for the first batch when the second batch was shipped, and Heilongjiang Company also failed to continue supplying the goods on time; both parties breached the contract, and they may not pursue liability for breach of contract against each other. This case only adjudicated the dispute over the purchase and sales contract among Chikan Company, Darong Company, and Heilongjiang Company. Whether there was a tort between Darong Company and Chikan Company was not within the scope of this case and should be dealt with in a separate action. Chikan Company's claims in the contract dispute action that Heilongjiang Company had not supplied the goods and its requests for an order that Heilongjiang Company return the prepayment of RMB 2,000,000 plus interest, pay liquidated damages, and compensate for losses lacked factual basis and legal grounds. Accordingly, on May 18, 1996, the Guangdong High People's Court entered a final judgment, affirming item 1 of the first-instance judgment, reversing items 2, 3, and 4, and instead dismissing Chikan Company's claims.

The above facts are confirmed by the civil judgments and trial transcripts of the Zhanjiang Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province and the Guangdong High People's Court.

Xinhua District People's Court of Haikou City held:

The steel billet purchase and sales contract and its modification agreement entered into by the plaintiff Chikan Company, the defendant Darong Company, and the defendant Heilongjiang Company were legally established and have legal effect. Chikan Company and Darong Company, as co-buyers under the contract, paid prepayments of RMB 2,000,000 and RMB 3,000,000 respectively, and the steel billets purchased by the parties should be jointly owned in proportion to the prepayments paid. Darong Company, by means of forged documents, unilaterally took delivery of 2,000 tons of steel billets and, after selling them, appropriated all the货款 for itself, which violated the principle of good faith in civil law and infringed upon the legitimate rights and interests of Chikan Company. Article 117, paragraph 1 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC provides: "Anyone who encroaches upon the property of the state, a collective, or another person shall return the property; if the property cannot be returned, it shall be compensated at its estimated price." Paragraph 3 provides: "If the victim suffers other major losses as a result, the infringer shall also compensate for those losses." Darong Company shall bear liability for compensation for the economic losses caused to Chikan Company by its infringing act.

The defendant Darong Company, by impersonating the plaintiff Chikan Company, entered into a purchase and sales contract with the defendant Heilongjiang Company for the first batch of 2,000 tons of steel billets, unilaterally increased the unit price of the steel billets, and settled accounts with Heilongjiang Company alone, paying an additional RMB 300,000 to Heilongjiang Company. This constituted a separate purchase and sales relationship between Darong Company and Heilongjiang Company, and the settlement consequences arising therefrom shall be borne by Darong Company itself.

Given that the final judgment of the Guangdong High People's Court has terminated the performance of the steel billet purchase and sales contract and its modification agreement, and that the defendant Darong Company has sold all 2,000 tons of steel billets, the prepayment of RMB 2,000,000 paid by the plaintiff Chikan Company and the interest that should be compensated for that amount by analogy with the provisions of the People's Bank of China on overdue payment shall be compensated by Darong Company to Chikan Company.

Since the defendant Heilongjiang Company did not commit any infringing act against the plaintiff Chikan Company, Chikan Company's request that Heilongjiang Company bear joint and several liability for compensation for the infringing act of the defendant Darong Company is not supported. Chikan Company's request that Darong Company and Heilongjiang Company jointly compensate for the expenses of RMB 172,400 incurred in pursuing the goods and the money is not supported because Chikan Company failed to provide evidence for this claim. Chikan Company's request for a finding that Heilongjiang Company breached the contract and for compensation for losses at 5% of the total contract amount has already been adjudicated by the Guangdong High People's Court. This request is not within the scope of this case and is not adjudicated.

After learning that the defendant Darong Company had received the 2,000 tons of steel billets, the plaintiff Chikan Company filed a lawsuit with the Zhanjiang Intermediate People's Court on December 15, 1993. The facts alleged in that lawsuit were the same as those in the present lawsuit. That case was concluded on May 18, 1996, after two trials. The final judgment of the Guangdong High People's Court clearly stated that the case only adjudicated the dispute over the purchase and sales contract that Chikan Company had sued on and did not adjudicate the tort facts that Chikan Company had alleged. Since Chikan Company had submitted the tort facts to the court, the statute of limitations was naturally interrupted until a legally effective judgment was obtained. After receiving the final judgment of the Guangdong High People's Court that the tort facts should be dealt with in a separate action, Chikan Company filed this tort compensation lawsuit against Darong Company in January 1997, which did not exceed the statutory limitation period. Darong Company's defense that Chikan Company's lawsuit exceeded the statute of limitations is untenable.

In summary, Xinhua District People's Court of Haikou City entered the following judgment:

1. Within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, the defendant Darong Company shall compensate the plaintiff Chikan Company for the prepayment of RMB 2,000,000 and interest losses. (Method of calculating interest losses: from May 12, 1993, until the performance period specified in this judgment, at a daily rate of 0.05%). If performance is delayed, the debt interest for the period of delayed performance shall be paid at double the highest loan interest rate of the bank for the same period.
2. The other claims of the plaintiff Chikan Company are dismissed.

Litigation costs of RMB 21,010 shall be borne by the defendant Darong Company.

After the first-instance judgment was announced, the defendant Darong Company, still relying on its original defense reasons, appealed to the Haikou Intermediate People's Court of Hainan Province.

Upon trial, the Haikou Intermediate People's Court held that the appellee Chikan Company and the appellant Darong Company, as co-buyers under the purchase and sales contract and the modification agreement, although they had not agreed on the distribution and sale of the goods upon arrival, should, in accordance with the principles of fairness and equivalent compensation that should be followed in civil activities, enjoy rights to the steel billets delivered by Heilongjiang Company in proportion to the prepayments each had paid. During the performance of the contract, Darong Company used forged documents to deceive others, unilaterally took delivery of the goods and sold them all, and appropriated all the proceeds for itself. Its conduct infringed upon the legitimate rights and interests of Chikan Company. Therefore, the first-instance court's determination that the above conduct of Darong Company constituted a tort and its order that Darong Company bear tortious civil liability were correct. Darong Company's grounds of appeal are all untenable. The first-instance judgment found the facts clearly, characterized the legal nature accurately, and the trial procedure was lawful. However, the order that Darong Company compensate Chikan Company for interest losses at a daily rate of 0.05% from May 12, 1993, was improper and should be corrected. Darong Company shall compensate Chikan Company for interest losses on the货款 at the deposit interest rate for the same period for institutional demand deposits prescribed by the People's Bank of China. Accordingly, the Haikou Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, entered the following judgment:

1. Affirm item 2 of the first-instance civil judgment;
2. Amend item 1 of the first-instance civil judgment to read: Darong Company shall, within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, return the full amount of Chikan Company's货款 of RMB 2,000,000 to Chikan Company, and shall pay the legal fruits of that amount at the demand deposit interest rate for institutions for the same period prescribed by the People's Bank of China. If Darong Company fails to pay the aforementioned amount when due, it shall pay debt interest for the period of delayed performance at double the highest loan interest rate for the same period prescribed by the People's Bank of China.

The litigation costs for the first instance and the second instance total RMB 42,020, of which RMB 12,606 shall be borne by Chikan Company and RMB 29,414 by Darong Company.
